subject: English Comprehension
text: The corporate team felt that the new project was too risky to undertake, so they decided to back down.
explanation: "Back out" means to withdraw from an agreement, commitment, or project. "Back down" means to admit defeat in an argument. Here, the context is about withdrawing from a project.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Scarcely had he reached the station than the train started.
explanation: According to the rule of correlative conjunctions, "Scarcely" and "Hardly" are followed by "when" or "before," not "than." "Than" is used with "No sooner."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is looking forward to meet her childhood friend after a decade.
explanation: The phrase "look forward to" is always followed by a gerund (Verb + ing), not by an infinitive (to + Verb).

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I was a king, I would help the poor and needy of my kingdom.
explanation: This is a hypothetical conditional sentence. In such imaginary situations, "were" is used for all subjects, whether singular or plural.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The teacher as well as her students are present in the seminar.
explanation: When subjects are connected by "as well as," "along with," or "together with," the verb agrees with the first subject. Since "The teacher" is singular, the correct verb is "is."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is senior than me in the digital marketing department.
explanation: Latin adjectives such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, and prior take the preposition "to" instead of "than."

subject: English Comprehension
text: I have been living in this chaotic city since five years.
explanation: "For" is used to indicate a period or duration of time, whereas "since" is used to indicate a specific point in time.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner did the bell ring when the children ran out of their classrooms.
explanation: The correlative conjunction "No sooner" is always followed by "than."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Unless you do not work hard, you cannot clear the Tier-2 exam.
explanation: "Unless" already carries a negative meaning equivalent to "if not." Therefore, using another negative word such as "not" is incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am tired with walking such a long distance in the sun.
explanation: The fixed expression is "tired of," which means exhausted or fed up because of an activity or situation.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Detailed dynamic reports are preparing by the analysis team this week.
explanation: The reports receive the action rather than perform it. Therefore, the sentence requires the Present Continuous Passive Voice form: "are being prepared."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He didn't know the answer, did he?
explanation: A negative statement takes a positive question tag. Since the sentence is negative ("didn't know"), the correct tag is "did he."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Every man and every woman have the right to express their opinion.
explanation: When singular nouns are preceded by "every" and joined by "and," they take a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It is high time we start saving money for our future expenses.
explanation: Expressions such as "It is high time" are followed by a verb in the past subjunctive form (V2).

subject: English Comprehension
text: Although he studied thoroughly, but he failed to secure the top rank.
explanation: "Although" and "but" should not be used together. "Although" may be followed by "yet," or the sentence can simply continue without "but."

subject: English Comprehension
text: If he had informed me earlier, I will have picked him up from the airport.
explanation: This is a third conditional sentence. If the "if-clause" contains "had + V3," the main clause should take "would have + V3."

subject: English Comprehension
text: By this time next year, she will complete her post-graduation degree.
explanation: The phrase "By this time next year" indicates that an action will be completed before a specific future time. Therefore, the Future Perfect Tense is required.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I have seen him yesterday at the shopping mall but he didn't see me.
explanation: "Yesterday" is a definite past time marker, so the Simple Past Tense should be used instead of the Present Perfect Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Suppose if you are selected for the post, which city would you prefer?
explanation: "Suppose" and "if" convey the same meaning. Using both together creates redundancy.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The water in the river is flowing over the danger mark since last evening.
explanation: The phrase "since last evening" indicates an action that began in the past and continues into the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He has had his lunch an hour ago.
explanation: "An hour ago" refers to a definite time in the past, so the Simple Past Tense should be used instead of the Present Perfect Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I wish I am the Prime Minister of this country to solve unemployment.
explanation: Sentences beginning with "I wish" express unreal or imaginary situations, and "were" is used for all subjects in such cases.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is having a luxurious car and a big house in Delhi.
explanation: "Have" is a stative verb when showing possession and is generally not used in continuous forms.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner did the thief see the police then he took to his heels.
explanation: The correlative conjunction "No sooner" is always followed by "than."

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I will win the lottery, I will buy a new house for my parents.
explanation: In the First Conditional, the if-clause takes the Simple Present Tense, while the main clause takes the Simple Future Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The train left the station before we arrived there.
explanation: When two actions occurred in the past, the action completed earlier takes the Past Perfect Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am looking forward to receive your reply soon.
explanation: "Look forward to" is followed by a gerund because "to" functions as a preposition in this expression.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is working in this company for the past ten years.
explanation: The duration phrase "for the past ten years" requires the Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The custom has been hard to root out because it is centuries old.
explanation: "Root out" is a phrasal verb meaning to eliminate something completely. The sentence is already correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It is raining heavily since morning, so the match was called off.
explanation: Since the cancellation of the match is described in the past, the ongoing action before that point should be expressed in the Past Perfect Continuous Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She told me that she will go to Mumbai the next day.
explanation: In indirect speech, if the reporting verb is in the past tense, "will" changes to "would."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is discrete while discussing confidential matters with clients.
explanation: "Discrete" means separate or distinct, whereas "discreet" means careful and tactful. The context requires "discreet."

subject: English Comprehension
text: You had better to consult a doctor before the condition worsens.
explanation: Expressions such as "had better," "would rather," and "let" are followed by the bare infinitive without "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The dynamic leader succeeded to capture the attention of the youth.
explanation: The verb "succeed" is followed by the preposition "in," and the verb after a preposition takes the gerund form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: When we reached the stadium, the players already started warming up.
explanation: The action of warming up occurred before we reached the stadium, so the Past Perfect Tense is required.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My brother does not smoke, nor he drinks.
explanation: Clauses beginning with "nor" require inversion, where the auxiliary verb comes before the subject.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I was you, I would never accept such a demotion.
explanation: In hypothetical or unreal conditional sentences, "were" is used instead of "was."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The scheme has lapsed due to lack of adequate government funding.
explanation: The Present Perfect structure "has lapsed" is correctly used to indicate that the scheme has come to an end.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He denied to assist me in finishing the official paperwork.
explanation: "Refuse" is followed by the infinitive form (to + verb) when declining a request. "Deny" is generally used to reject an accusation or admit not doing something.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I lay in bed all day yesterday suffering from a severe migraine.
explanation: The past tense of "lie" (to recline) is "lay." Since the sentence refers to yesterday, "lay" is correctly used.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Either the manager or his subordinates is responsible for this massive data breach.
explanation: In structures using "either...or" and "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. "Subordinates" is plural, so "are" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The furniture in this newly built apartment are made of high-quality teak wood.
explanation: "Furniture" is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: One of the student from our batch has cleared the UPSC civil services exam.
explanation: The correct structure is "One of + plural noun + singular verb."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Between you and I, I don't think this strategy will yield any profit.
explanation: Pronouns following prepositions must be in the objective case. Therefore, "me" is correct after "between."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Two-thirds of the book were ruined by the leakage in the roof.
explanation: When a fraction refers to a singular or uncountable noun, it takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Each of the participants were given a certificate of appreciation.
explanation: Expressions such as "each of" take singular verbs because they refer to individuals separately.

subject: English Comprehension
text: This is the same laptop which my father gifted me on my birthday.
explanation: After expressions such as "the same," "the only," and superlatives, the relative pronoun "that" is preferred.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Scarcely he had finished his speech when the audience broke into applause.
explanation: Negative adverbs placed at the beginning of a sentence require inversion of the auxiliary verb and subject.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The sceneries of Kashmir are absolutely breathtaking and mesmerizing.
explanation: "Scenery" is an uncountable noun and does not have a plural form. It takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He solved the mathematical puzzle more quicker than his classmate.
explanation: The verb "solved" should be modified by an adverb. The correct comparative form is "more quickly." Double comparatives such as "more quicker" are incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Whom do you think are going to win the man of the match award today?
explanation: The verb "are going to win" requires a subject pronoun. "Who" is used as a subject, whereas "whom" is used as an object.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Economics are considered a tough subject by many competitive exam aspirants.
explanation: Names of subjects such as Economics, Mathematics, and Physics appear plural but are treated as singular and take singular verbs.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It was him who stood by me during my financial crisis.
explanation: After expressions like "It is" or "It was," the pronoun should be in the subjective case. Therefore, "he" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My sister-in-laws have invited us to celebrate the festival together.
explanation: In compound nouns, the principal word takes the plural form. Therefore, the plural of "sister-in-law" is "sisters-in-law."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Neither of the two candidates were found suitable for the executive profile.
explanation: "Neither of" is treated as singular and therefore requires a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The cattle is grazing peacefully in the green pasture down the valley.
explanation: "Cattle" is a collective noun used in a plural sense and always takes a plural verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The jury were unanimous in its final decision regarding the verdict.
explanation: When a collective noun acts as a single unit and expresses unanimity, it takes a singular verb and singular pronoun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He behaves as if he knows everything about quantum astrophysics.
explanation: "As if" and "as though" expressing unreal situations are followed by the past subjunctive form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I bought two dozens bananas from the local street vendor.
explanation: After definite numerals such as two, three, and four, words like dozen, hundred, and thousand remain singular, while the following noun remains plural.

subject: English Comprehension
text: This is the boy whom I know saved the drowning child yesterday.
explanation: The relative pronoun functions as the subject of the verb "saved," so "who" is required instead of "whom."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Five thousand rupees are a large sum for a poor laborer to arrange.
explanation: A sum of money, distance, weight, or period considered as a single unit takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Every student should submit their assignment before Friday evening.
explanation: "Every student" is singular; therefore, according to traditional grammar rules, it should take a singular possessive pronoun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The quality of these mangoes are not up to the export standards.
explanation: The real subject of the sentence is "The quality," which is singular and requires a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is one of those men who does not compromise on moral principles.
explanation: The relative pronoun "who" refers to "men," which is plural; therefore, the plural verb "do" should be used.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My scissors is missing from the study table drawer.
explanation: Nouns such as scissors, trousers, spectacles, and tongs are plural in form and take plural verbs. However, "a pair of scissors" takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Of the two smart variants, this smartphone is the best option.
explanation: When comparing only two persons or things, the Comparative Degree is used. The Superlative Degree is used when comparing more than two.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is enough wise to understand the cunning political trap.
explanation: The adverb "enough" is placed after the adjective it modifies. Therefore, the correct structure is "adjective + enough."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She was so infuriated that she slammed the cabin door heavy.
explanation: The verb "slammed" should be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. Hence, "heavily" is the correct choice.

subject: English Comprehension
text: This task is preferable than the one assigned to me last week.
explanation: The adjective "preferable" is followed by the preposition "to," not "than." It should not be preceded by "more."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The climate of Bengaluru is much better than Delhi.
explanation: Comparisons should be made between similar entities. The climate of Bengaluru should be compared with the climate of Delhi, not with the city itself.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He ran as fastly as he could to catch the last metro train.
explanation: "Fast" functions as both an adjective and an adverb. The word "fastly" is incorrect in standard English.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I cannot cope up with this tremendous working pressure anymore.
explanation: The correct idiomatic expression is "cope with," which means to deal successfully with a difficult situation.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The aggressive dog was angry on the postman who entered the gate.
explanation: "Angry with" is used when referring to a person, whereas "angry at" is generally used for situations or things.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He abstained from voting in the local municipal elections.
explanation: The verb "abstain" is correctly followed by the preposition "from" and a gerund form of the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is the most unique singer I have ever heard in live concerts.
explanation: Adjectives such as "unique," "perfect," and "complete" express absolute qualities and generally do not take comparative or superlative forms.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He has hardly some money left in his bank account after the premium payment.
explanation: Words such as "hardly," "barely," and "scarcely" carry a negative sense and are followed by "any," not "some."

subject: English Comprehension
text: No other metal is as useful than iron in heavy industrial manufacturing.
explanation: The correct structure for positive degree comparison is "as + adjective + as."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is too intelligent that he cannot be fooled easily by online scammers.
explanation: The structure "so + adjective + that + clause" is used to express cause and result. "Too...to" requires an infinitive rather than a clause.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The dynamic young officer was invested with the power of magistrate.
explanation: The expression "invested with" means to formally confer authority, power, or responsibility upon someone. The sentence is grammatically correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I will go to Delhi, I will bring your books.
explanation: In the First Conditional, the if-clause takes the Simple Present Tense, while the main clause takes the Simple Future Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The standard of living in India is lower than England.
explanation: The comparison is between the standard of living in India and the standard of living in England. "That of" avoids repetition of the singular noun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Neither the principal nor the lecturers was present in the meeting.
explanation: In "Neither...nor" constructions, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. Since "lecturers" is plural, "were" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He did not know how to solve the problem, and neither I did.
explanation: Negative agreement requires inversion after "neither," placing the auxiliary verb before the subject.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The criminal was hung to death this morning.
explanation: "Hanged" is used when referring to execution by hanging, whereas "hung" is used for suspending objects.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is having a luxurious car and a big house in Mumbai.
explanation: Stative verbs expressing possession are generally not used in continuous forms.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My brother-in-laws who live in London have come to visit us.
explanation: In compound nouns, the principal word takes the plural form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am working on this research project since January.
explanation: Since an action started in the past and continues to the present, the Present Perfect Continuous Tense is required.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner had he finished his speech when the audience started clapping.
explanation: "No sooner" is always paired with "than."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a students have failed the physical endurance test.
explanation: "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is too weak that he cannot walk without support.
explanation: The correct structure is "too + adjective + to + verb."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She handles all tasks with carefully.
explanation: The verb should be modified by an adverb. "Carefully" is the appropriate form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: You must avail yourself of this golden opportunity.
explanation: The correct expression is "avail oneself of," which requires a reflexive pronoun followed by "of."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The weather of Mussoorie conduces for good health.
explanation: The verb "conduce" is followed by the preposition "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Suppose if you are selected, which city would you prefer?
explanation: "Suppose" and "if" convey the same meaning, so using both together is redundant.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is the most cleverest boy in our class.
explanation: "Cleverest" is already a superlative form. Using "most" creates an incorrect double superlative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The short-circuit caused a major damage to the server room.
explanation: "Damage" is an uncountable noun in this context and does not take the article "a."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Unless you do not apologize, you will be suspended.
explanation: "Unless" already implies negation, so an additional negative form is unnecessary.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I bought two dozens bananas from the local vendor.
explanation: After definite numerals, words such as dozen, hundred, and thousand remain singular.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The manager disposed off the old files within an hour.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is "dispose of," meaning to get rid of something.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Let you and I complete this assignment together.
explanation: "Let" is followed by objective pronouns such as me, him, her, and us.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It is high time you take up a serious job.
explanation: The expression "It is high time" is followed by a verb in the past subjunctive form (V2).

subject: English Comprehension
text: Bread and butter are a wholesome breakfast for athletes.
explanation: When two nouns together express a single idea or one item, they take a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The custom officer scarcely entered the room than the lights went out.
optionA: had scarcely entered the room when
optionB: scarcely had entered the room than
explanation: "Scarcely" is commonly used with the Past Perfect Tense and is followed by "when."

subject: English Comprehension
text: This is the most unique piece of art I have ever seen.
explanation: "Unique" is an absolute adjective and does not normally take comparative or superlative forms.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is good in Mathematics but weak in English.
explanation: The correct expression for being skilled in a subject or activity is "good at."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The committee were unanimous in its decision.
explanation: A collective noun expressing a unified opinion takes a singular verb and singular pronoun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Each of the participants were given a certificate.
explanation: Expressions such as "each of" take singular verbs because they refer to individuals separately.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The news of the plane crash are shocking.
explanation: "News" is singular in form and meaning and therefore takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He walked fast lest he should not miss the train.
explanation: "Lest" itself conveys a negative meaning and is followed by "should" without "not."

subject: English Comprehension
text: One should perform his duty sincerely.
explanation: When the subject is "one," the corresponding possessive pronoun should be "one's."

subject: English Comprehension
text: I look forward to receive your reply soon.
explanation: The phrase "look forward to" is followed by a gerund because "to" functions as a preposition.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The master severe punished the servant for breaking the vase.
explanation: The verb should be modified by an adverb. Therefore, "severely" is required instead of the adjective "severe."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She prefers tea than coffee in the morning.
explanation: The verb "prefer" is followed by the preposition "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The Scenery of Kashmir are very beautiful.
explanation: "Scenery" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Hard work is the key for success.
explanation: The fixed expression is "the key to success."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He has completed his graduation in 2022.
explanation: A definite past time expression requires the Simple Past Tense rather than the Present Perfect Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I cannot agree with your proposal.
explanation: We "agree with" a person but "agree to" a proposal, suggestion, or plan.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Being a rainy day, I decided to stay indoors.
optionA: It being a rainy day, I decided to stay
optionB: As it being a rainy day, I decided to stay
optionC: Since a rainy day, I decided to stay
explanation: The original sentence contains a dangling participle. The introductory phrase requires its own logical subject, "It."

subject: English Comprehension
text: They left the hotel with bag and baggage.
explanation: "Bag and baggage" is a fixed idiomatic expression, and adding "with" before it is unnecessary.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If he had studied hard, he would pass the exam.
explanation: The Third Conditional follows the pattern: If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The click of the cameras distracted the batsman.
explanation: The singular subject "click" correctly takes the Simple Past verb "distracted."

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner did I opened the door than the cat ran out.
explanation: After auxiliary verbs such as "did," the base form of the verb is used.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The performance of our team was much better than expected.
explanation: "Much better" is a correct way to emphasize a comparative adjective. "More better" is incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Both the sisters are not going to the party.
explanation: To express a negative idea involving two people, "neither of" with a singular verb is preferred.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The fire spread across the building but fortunately everyone could escape.
explanation: "Was able to" is often preferred for describing successful completion of a specific action in the past.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a man have lost everything in gambling.
explanation: "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He behaves as if he is the owner of the company.
explanation: Unreal or hypothetical situations introduced by "as if" take the past subjunctive form "were."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Beside his parents, his uncle was also present at the function.
explanation: "Besides" means "in addition to," whereas "beside" means "next to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The climate of Chennai is hotter than Bangalore.
explanation: The comparison should be between the climates of the two cities, not between a climate and a city.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is senior and older than all other employees in this office.
explanation: "Senior" is followed by "to," while "older" is followed by "than." Each adjective must take its correct preposition.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My friend is habituated to smoke after dinner.
explanation: Expressions such as "habituated to," "accustomed to," and "used to" are followed by a gerund (verb + ing form).

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner the thief saw the police than he took to his heels.
optionA: No sooner did the thief see
optionB: No sooner had the thief saw
optionC: No sooner the thief had seen
explanation: Sentences beginning with "No sooner" require inversion. The auxiliary verb comes before the subject, and "did" is followed by the base form of the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is the prettiest of the two sisters.
optionC: more pretty of the two sisters
explanation: When comparing only two persons or things, the comparative degree should be used instead of the superlative degree.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I would rather die to beg.
explanation: The correct structure is "would rather + base verb + than + base verb."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The teacher asked the student why was he late.
explanation: In indirect speech, interrogative sentences change into assertive word order, placing the subject before the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He has not seen his parents since two years.
explanation: "For" is used to indicate a duration of time, whereas "since" refers to a specific point in time.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The match had started before we reached the stadium.
explanation: The earlier past action takes the Past Perfect Tense, while the later action takes the Simple Past Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The news are true; I heard it on the radio.
explanation: "News" is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: You cannot bypass the rules, can you?
explanation: A negative statement requires a positive question tag. The given tag is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is enough wise to understand your tricks.
explanation: The word "enough" follows the adjective it modifies.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The Cattle is grazing in the nearby meadows.
explanation: "Cattle" is treated as a plural noun and therefore takes a plural verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: They are discussing about the new economic policy.
explanation: "Discuss" is a transitive verb and does not require the preposition "about."

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I was you, I would accept the job offer immediately.
explanation: Hypothetical or unreal conditions require the subjunctive form "were."

subject: English Comprehension
text: None of the two candidates is eligible for the post.
optionC: No one of the two candidates
explanation: "Neither" is used for two persons or things, whereas "none" is generally used for more than two.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He ordered for a cup of strong filter coffee.
explanation: "Order" is a transitive verb and does not require the preposition "for."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Unless you do not study hard, you will fail.
explanation: Since "unless" already expresses a negative meaning, an additional negative form is incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Each of the employees have received the bonus.
explanation: Expressions such as "each of" take singular verbs.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She behaves as if she knows everything.
explanation: Unreal present situations after "as if" often take the past subjunctive form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It is high time you return home.
explanation: The expression "It is high time" is followed by a past tense verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is addicted to gamble.
explanation: "Addicted to" is followed by a gerund.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is more cleverer than her brother.
explanation: Using both "more" and a comparative form creates an incorrect double comparative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am tired with doing the same repetitive task everyday.
explanation: The correct expression is "tired of."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The population of Tokyo is greater than any city in the world.
optionA: than that of any other city
explanation: The comparison should be between populations, not between a population and a city.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a soldier have lost their lives in the war.
explanation: "Many a" takes a singular noun, singular verb, and singular pronoun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Scarcely had I opened the umbrella than it started raining heavily.
explanation: "Scarcely" is correctly paired with "when."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The furniture in this showroom are made of high-quality teak wood.
explanation: "Furniture" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Both of them did not go to the exhibition.
explanation: For two people in a negative context, "neither of" is preferred.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Hard work is the key for success.
explanation: The correct expression is "the key to success."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He walked fast lest he should miss the bus.
explanation: "Lest" is correctly followed by "should" without an additional negative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: One must respect his elders.
explanation: The possessive form corresponding to "one" is "one's."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The standard of education in private schools is better than government schools.
explanation: The comparison is between standards of education, not the schools themselves.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He entered into the room without any permission.
explanation: The verb "enter" does not require the preposition "into."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The performance of the actors was majorly superior than yesterday.
explanation: Adjectives such as superior, inferior, senior, and junior are followed by "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: I prefer swimming than running.
explanation: The verb "prefer" takes the preposition "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Being a fine day, we went out for a long drive.
optionA: It being a fine day, we went out
optionB: As being a fine day, we went out
optionC: Since fine day, we went out
explanation: The introductory phrase requires its own logical subject to avoid a dangling participle.

subject: English Comprehension
text: They left the town with bag and baggage.
explanation: "Bag and baggage" is a fixed idiomatic expression.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I had known you were in town, I would have met you.
explanation: The sentence correctly follows the Third Conditional pattern.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He was hung for the murder of his business partner.
explanation: "Hanged" is used in the context of execution by hanging.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Neither the teacher nor the students was happy with the new timetable.
explanation: The verb agrees with the subject nearest to it, which is plural.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He did not pass the exam, and neither did his sister.
explanation: The sentence correctly follows the inversion pattern used after "neither."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is owning three prime properties in Delhi NCR.
explanation: "Own" is a stative verb and is generally not used in continuous forms to indicate possession.

subject: English Comprehension
text: My sister-in-las have come to stay with us.
explanation: The plural form of this compound noun is created by pluralizing the principal noun.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am preparing for SSC CGL since five months.
explanation: An action continuing over a period of time requires the Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is too weak that he cannot lift this heavy box.
explanation: The structure "so + adjective + that + clause" is appropriate here.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She manages the financial accounts with carefully.
explanation: The verb should be modified by an adverb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: You must avail of this opportunity to excel.
explanation: The correct expression is "avail yourself of."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The pleasant climate of Bengaluru conduces for good health.
explanation: The verb "conduce" is followed by the preposition "to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Suppose if you lose the match, what will you do?
explanation: Using both "suppose" and "if" together is redundant.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Bread and butter are my favorite breakfast item.
explanation: When two nouns refer to a single item or idea, a singular verb is used.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is the most unique designer in the fashion industry.
explanation: "Unique" is an absolute adjective and should not be used with superlative forms.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is good in making intricate sketches.
explanation: The fixed expression "good at" is used to indicate skill or proficiency in an activity or subject. Therefore, "good at making intricate sketches" is the correct usage.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The panel were unanimous in its final verdict.
explanation: A collective noun such as "panel" takes a singular verb when the members act as a single unit. Since the panel was unanimous, the singular verb "was" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Each of the participants were rewarded with a memento.
explanation: "Each of" is treated as singular and therefore requires a singular verb. Hence, "was rewarded" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The news of his sudden demise are not yet confirmed.
explanation: "News" is an uncountable noun that always takes a singular verb. Therefore, "is not yet confirmed" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Run fast lest you should not miss the train.
explanation: The conjunction "lest" already carries a negative meaning. Therefore, "not" should not be used after it. The correct structure is "lest + subject + should + base verb."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Every citizen must perform his duty towards the nation.
explanation: In traditional grammar, "his" is acceptable as a singular possessive pronoun referring to "every citizen." Therefore, the sentence is considered correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am looking forward to meet the delegates tomorrow.
explanation: The phrase "look forward to" is followed by a gerund (verb + ing), not an infinitive. Hence, "to meeting" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The manager severely punished the clerk for breaking the rules.
explanation: The adverb "severely" correctly modifies the verb "punished." Therefore, the sentence is grammatically correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I prefer corporate life than a government job.
explanation: The verb "prefer" is followed by the preposition "to" when comparing two alternatives.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The sceneries of Switzerland are mesmerizing.
explanation: "Scenery" is an uncountable noun and does not have a plural form. It also takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Hard work is the key for cracking competitive exams.
explanation: The correct expression is "the key to" followed by a noun or gerund.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He has passed his examination three years ago.
explanation: When a definite past time expression such as "three years ago" is used, the Simple Past Tense is required instead of the Present Perfect Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The committee cannot agree with this controversial proposal.
explanation: We "agree with" a person but "agree to" a proposal, plan, or suggestion.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Being a stormy night, the sailor anchored the ship.
optionA: It being a stormy night, the sailor anchored
optionB: As being a stormy night, the sailor anchored
optionC: Since a stormy night, the sailor anchored
explanation: The introductory phrase lacks a proper subject. "It" should be used to refer to the weather condition.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The refugees escaped with bag and baggage.
explanation: The idiom is "bag and baggage." Since the meaning of "with" is already implied, the extra "with" should be removed.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If they had played well, they would win the match.
explanation: This is a Third Conditional sentence. The structure is: If + had + V3, subject + would have + V3.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The continuous ticking of the clocks distracted the students.
explanation: The subject "The continuous ticking" is singular, and the sentence correctly uses the Simple Past Tense.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner did the teacher entered the room than the students stood up.
explanation: After "did," the base form of the verb must be used. Therefore, "enter" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Her performance was much better than mine.
explanation: "Much better" is a correct comparative structure used for emphasis. "More better" would be an incorrect double comparative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Both the layout designs are not suitable for the magazine cover.
optionA: Neither of the layout designs is
optionB: None of the layout designs are
explanation: For two items in a negative sense, "Neither of" followed by a singular verb is the correct structure.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The fire spread rapidly but everyone could evacuate safely.
explanation: "Was able to" is preferred when referring to successful completion of a specific action in the past.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a man have lost fortunes in stock market speculation.
explanation: "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. Therefore, "has lost" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She talks as if she is the prime minister.
explanation: "As if" introducing an unreal situation generally requires the subjunctive form "were."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Beside his business, he manages an NGO as well.
explanation: "Besides" means "in addition to," whereas "beside" means "next to."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The climate of Shimla is cooler than Delhi.
explanation: The comparison is between the climates of two places. "That of" avoids repetition of the noun "climate."

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is senior and older than me.
explanation: "Senior" takes the preposition "to," whereas "older" takes "than."

subject: English Comprehension
text: My friend is habituated to drive fast on highways.
explanation: Expressions such as "habituated to" are followed by a gerund.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner the alarm rang than he jumped out of bed.
optionA: No sooner did the alarm ring
optionB: No sooner had the alarm rang
optionC: No sooner the alarm had rung
explanation: Sentences beginning with "No sooner" require inversion. "Did" is followed by the base form of the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is the most intelligent of the two brothers.
optionA: more intelligent of the two brothers
optionB: most intelligent between the two brothers
explanation: When comparing only two people or things, the comparative degree should be used instead of the superlative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I would rather fail to copy in exams.
explanation: The structure is "would rather + V1 + than + V1."

subject: English Comprehension
text: The officer asked the clerk why was he editing the logs.
explanation: In indirect speech, the interrogative structure changes to the statement order: Wh-word + subject + verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: They have been planning this venture since six months.
explanation: "For" is used with a period of time, whereas "since" is used with a specific point of time.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The concert had ended before we had entered the auditorium.
explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier action takes the Past Perfect, while the later action takes the Simple Past.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The information provided by the agent were completely false.
explanation: "Information" is an uncountable noun and therefore takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: You will not attend the function, will you?
explanation: A negative statement requires a positive question tag. The sentence already follows the correct rule.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is enough tall to reach the upper shelf.
explanation: "Enough" follows the adjective it modifies. Therefore, "tall enough" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The Gentry of this locality is highly educated.
explanation: "Gentry" is treated as a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The researchers are investigating about the viral outbreak.
explanation: "Investigate" is a transitive verb and does not require the preposition "about."

subject: English Comprehension
text: If I was a millionaire, I would fund this research.
explanation: Hypothetical or unreal conditions require the subjunctive form "were."

subject: English Comprehension
text: None of the two choices is correct.
optionC: No one of the two choices
explanation: When referring to only two items in a negative sense, "Neither" is preferred over "None."

subject: English Comprehension
text: She ordered for a new smartphone online.
explanation: "Order" is a transitive verb and takes its object directly without the preposition "for."

subject: English Comprehension
text: Unless you do not pay the fine, you won't get your documents.
explanation: "Unless" already expresses a negative meaning. Therefore, an additional "not" is incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Each of the projects have unique challenges.
explanation: "Each of" requires a singular verb because the focus is on each individual item.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He behaves as if he rules the entire country.
explanation: Unreal present situations introduced by "as if" generally take the past subjunctive form.

subject: English Comprehension
text: It is high time you confess the truth.
explanation: The expression "It is high time" is followed by the past subjunctive, using the second form of the verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is addicted to alcohol.
explanation: "Addicted to" may be followed by either a noun or a gerund. The sentence is already correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She is more smarter than her classmates.
explanation: "Smarter" is already a comparative form. Using "more" with it creates an incorrect double comparative.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The traveler was tired with the hectic journey.
explanation: The fixed expression is "tired of" when referring to weariness caused by a thing or situation.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The population of India is greater than any country in Asia.
optionA: than that of any other country
explanation: The comparison is between populations, not countries. "That of" avoids repetition, and "other" excludes India from the comparison group.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a student have registered for the online mock test.
explanation: "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. Therefore, "has registered" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Scarcely had the match started than it began to rain cats and dogs.
explanation: The correlative conjunction used with "Scarcely" and "Hardly" is "when" (or sometimes "before"), not "than". Therefore, "than" should be replaced with "when".

subject: English Comprehension
text: The logistics manager disposed off the damaged goods.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is "dispose of", which means to get rid of or discard something. "Dispose off" is incorrect.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Let you and I investigate the matter thoroughly.
explanation: After "let", objective case pronouns are used. Therefore, "I" should be replaced with "me".

subject: English Comprehension
text: Either the operator or the engineers has made a critical error.
explanation: In "Either...or" constructions, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. Since "engineers" is plural, the correct verb is "have".

subject: English Comprehension
text: He is too lazy that he cannot complete the project on time.
explanation: The structure "so + adjective + that + clause" is correct. "Too...to" cannot be followed by a clause containing "cannot".

subject: English Comprehension
text: The equipment in the chemistry lab are outdated.
explanation: "Equipment" is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I am more superior than him in technical skills.
explanation: "Superior" is followed by the preposition "to" and does not take "more" because it already expresses comparison.

subject: English Comprehension
text: I have been preparing this financial sheet since three hours.
explanation: "For" is used to indicate a duration of time, whereas "since" refers to a specific point in time.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The pricing of this product is cheaper than that brand.
explanation: The comparison is between the pricing of two brands, not between a price and a brand itself. Therefore, "that of" is required.

subject: English Comprehension
text: He entered into the laboratory without wearing a safety mask.
explanation: The verb "enter" itself means "go into", so using "into" after it is redundant.

subject: English Comprehension
text: Both the management and the staff is working together.
explanation: "Both...and" creates a plural subject, so it requires a plural verb.

subject: English Comprehension
text: The project was delayed due to the team didn't cooperate.
explanation: "Due to" and "because of" are followed by noun phrases, whereas "because" introduces a clause.

subject: English Comprehension
text: No sooner did the meeting end when the power went out.
explanation: The fixed correlative conjunction is "No sooner...than".

subject: English Comprehension
text: Many a candidate has applied for the assistant post.
explanation: "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb. The sentence is already correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: She handles every customer query with professionally.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb "handles". Therefore, "professionally" is correct.

subject: English Comprehension
text: This is the most perfect design for the corporate logo.
explanation: "Perfect" is an absolute adjective and does not take comparative or superlative forms such as "more" or "most".

subject: English Comprehension
text: The data provided by the department is verified.
explanation: In modern English usage, "data" is often treated as a singular mass noun, making "is verified" acceptable.

subject: English Comprehension
text: If he would have worked hard, he would have passed Tier-2.
explanation: In the Third Conditional, the if-clause takes the Past Perfect tense, while the main clause uses "would have + past participle".

subject: English Comprehension
text: One must be honest to his profession.
explanation: When the subject is "One", the corresponding possessive pronoun should be "one's".

subject: English Comprehension
text: The standard of living in metros is superior than rural areas.
explanation: The adjective "superior" is always followed by "to". Also, the comparison is between standards of living, so "that in" is required to avoid faulty comparison.
